This is a Craftsman 17" Dual Rotating Tine (DRT) Rear-Tine Tiller powered by a 7.0 HP gas engine (typically an OHV Briggs & Stratton or Kohler engine, model series often beginning with 917.xxxxx or 247.xxxxx).

Key Specifications & Features visible:

  • Tilling Width: 17 inches
  • Engine Power: 7.0 Horsepower
  • Tine Action: Dual Rotating Tines (DRT) — capable of running in forward rotation (CRT) for standard cultivation or counter-rotation (FRT/DRT) for breaking hard, compacted sod.
  • Depth Stake / Drag Bar: Controlled via the spring-loaded lever mechanism mounted on top of the tine shield to adjust tilling depth.
  • Tires: Heavy-duty agricultural lug tires for traction in loose or muddy soil.

turns.prompt_text: There is a hole opening with a plug at about the center of this image on this machine. We are unsure of what goes in it Attached 1 file. - 41078c99-a81f-4d0f-a218-1f9e2baf8e7d
turns.response_html:
That opening is the engine oil fill and check port (crankcase fill neck).

What goes in it:

  • Fluid: 4-cycle engine motor oil (typically SAE 30 for warm weather/tilling season, or 10W-30 multi-grade). Do not put mixed 2-stroke gas or fuel into this opening.
  • Component: A threaded oil fill cap / dipstick plug (usually yellow or black plastic with a rubber O-ring seal).

Important points:

  • Do not run the engine without the cap: Running it open will splash oil everywhere and allow dirt/dust from tilling directly into the crankcase, which will quickly destroy the piston and cylinder.
  • Fill Level: With the tiller parked on level ground, the oil level should typically reach the top threads of that fill neck (or to the "FULL" mark on the dipstick if equipped).

turns.prompt_text: This yellow Port seems to be the oil fill and not the previous one Attached 1 file. - e43f615c-d0d7-4bac-adb2-2287f6bfc9e6
turns.response_html:
Both ports actually lead to the exact same engine crankcase.

Small horizontal-shaft Briggs & Stratton OHV engines are designed for universal use across different machines (tillers, log splitters, pressure washers, generators). Because equipment frames and belt guards can block access on one side, Briggs casts dual oil fill ports into opposite sides of the engine base.

  • The Yellow Cap: This is the primary oil fill plug and dipstick. You will use this to fill the engine and check your oil level.
  • The Open Port (from the previous photo): This is the engine's auxiliary/secondary oil fill port on the opposite side of the crankcase.

Important: Even though you fill and check using the yellow dipstick, that open port from the first photo must be capped with a threaded plug before starting the engine. If left open, engine crankcase pressure will blow oil out and suck dirt/debris directly into the engine while running.
